Great — here’s a classic tricky exam-style question that exposes this confusion. 🧠 Tricky Question Given episode: (1,1) --left--> r = -2 (2,1) --up--> r = +3 (1,1) --right--> r = +5 (1,1) --left--> r = +4 terminal Assume: γ = 1 Use First-Visit Monte Carlo ❓ What to compute? Find which returns are used for: Q ((1,1),left) Q ((1,1),right) 🔍 Step 1: Identify occurrences (1,1), left appears: 1. First occurrence → at start ✅ 2. Second occurrence → later ❌ (ignore in first-visit) (1,1), right appears: Only once → ✅ use it 🔍 Step 2: Compute returns (backward helps) 🔹 For (1,1), left (FIRST occurrence only) From beginning: G = −2 + 3 + 5 + 4 = 10 👉 Use this for: Q ((1,1),left) = 10 🔹 For (1,1), right From that step: G = 5 + 4 = 9 👉 Use this for: Q ((1,1),right) = 9 ❌ Common Mistakes (VERY IMPORTANT) ❌ Mistake 1: “Ignore second visit of state (1,1) entirely” 👉 WRONG ✔ You only ignore repeated (1,1, left) , not (1,1, right) ❌ Mistake 2: Mixing actions together 👉 WRONG ✔ Each (state, action) is separate 🔥 Final Answer State-Action Return used (1,1), left 10 (1,1), right 9 🧠 Key Insight First-Visit applies to (state, action) pair, not just state 🚀 Exam One-liner In first-visit Monte Carlo, different actions from the same state are treated independently, and only the first occurrence of each state-action pair is used. Good catch — this is a subtle but very important point . 🧠 Your confusion “Why did we include the second (1,1) step if it’s a repeat?” ✅ Key Rule (VERY IMPORTANT) First-Visit decides which (s,a) to UPDATE — not which rewards to INCLUDE 🔥 What this means Even if a state-action pair repeats: ❌ We do NOT use it again for updating ✅ But we DO include its reward when computing return G 📦 Your example again (1,1) --left--> r = -2 (2,1) --up--> r = +3 (1,1) --right--> r = +5 (1,1) --left--> r = +4 terminal 🔹 For first (1,1), left We compute return: G = −2 + 3 + 5 + 4 👉 Why include the last +4? Because: It is part of the future trajectory after the first visit ⚠️ Important distinction Concept What it affects First-Visit Which (s,a) we update G Return All future rewards till terminal ❌ What you were thinking “Since (1,1,left) repeats, ignore everything after it” 👉 That would break the definition of return 🧠 Correct intuition “Once I take an action, I care about EVERYTHING that happens after it” Even if: same state repeats same action repeats 🚀 One-line exam answer In first-visit Monte Carlo, repeated occurrences of a state-action pair are ignored for updating, but all subsequent rewards are still included in the return calculation. ⚡ Memory trick Ignore repeat for updating, NOT for reward calculation If you want next: I can give a very tricky MCQ where this exact confusion is tested .
